Long-rumoured, Apple is developing a brand-new all-glass iPhone design to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone next year, but analysts at Jefferies believe the project is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analysts say a major redesign to mark the iPhone's 20th anniversary has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies has today downgraded its rating on Apple stock to "Underperform", with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that the possible cancellation of the 20th-anniversary edition iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons for the move.

The key to this downgrade lies in the suspected cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although reports as early as 2025 indicated the project was in development, with rumours suggesting a launch as soon as 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, the company did quietly file a patent application back in 2019 for what it called a "six-sided glass enclosure". Jefferies had at one point believed the launch of an all-glass iPhone was feasible, but Lee believes the development work has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply-chain checks indicate the project was scrapped due to poor yield rates. Lee views this decision as "a major setback for pushing higher-priced iPhones as memory costs rise". If the new device were to launch on schedule in September 2027 to mark the iPhone's 20th anniversary, he estimates its blended retail price would reach US$2,060 — higher than the average selling price of any model to date. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further driving up their average selling prices and profit margins." He sees this as an important defensive strategy at a time when memory prices are climbing.

Lee also noted that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are other reasons behind the downgrade of the company's stock rating.

From Lee's report, it cannot be determined whether the analyst believes the entire redesign has been shelved, or merely that certain details have been cancelled.

The most upvoted comment came from bcom77

It won't be long — perhaps in the not-too-distant future — there will come a tipping point where prices get so absurdly high that consumers simply stop buying new products. Unless the big tech companies start seriously addressing component costs, profit margins will begin to slide sharply. They have no way to keep passing the costs on to consumers.

For example, there have long been rumours that Apple will be unable to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. As a result, a truly "all-glass" display will not be possible. That said, the rumoured four-sided curved design may still see the light of day.

In any event, if Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone design has indeed been cancelled, other credible sources are expected to corroborate the news in the short term.
